title: OnsiteGene Nasal Direct Protocol
author: yliu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bkudkws6
materials: Ensure all collection materials are labelled with the correct identifying information.

steps.title: Prepare for Sample Collection
steps.instruction: Prepare the environment and personal protective equipment before collecting the sample.

substeps.instruction: Clean hands using alcohol-based sanitizer or soap and water (no fragrances).
Wear appropriate PPE (at minimum, gloves and a mask).
Back away as far as possible from the sample donor during the whole process.
Direct the sample donor to begin blowing nose softly while preparing collection materials.

steps.title: Collect Anterior Nasal Swab
steps.instruction: Collect the nasal sample with the assistance of a healthcare worker or technician.

substeps.instruction: Take the swab out from the package.
Insert swab into each nasal passage and rotate it against the inner nasal lining in a circle three times (insert only until the tip is no longer visible).

steps.title: Secure Sample in Storage Solution
steps.instruction: Place the collected swab into the provided storage solution.

substeps.instruction: Remove the lid of the collection tube containing 200 µL OnsiteGene sample storage solution.
Place the swab into the storage solution in the tube.
Remove the stick through the opening point, leaving the swab pad in the tube.
Discard the stick and secure the lid.

steps.title: Transport and Initial Processing
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample for RNA release.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the sample at room temperature for processing (virus RNA remains stable at room temperature for 3-5 days).
Vortex each sample collection tube for 5 seconds at 3000-5000 RPM (alternatively, tap or shake each tube to mix).

steps.title: Extract Viral RNA
steps.instruction: Release the viral RNA using the direct RNA release buffer and heat.

substeps.instruction: Spin down the tube for 15 seconds using a centrifuge to remove liquid from the cap and spin solid particles to the bottom.
Transfer 20 µL supernatant of the sample storage solution to a tube containing 20 µL SA TM direct RNA release buffer.
Secure the lid of the tube.
Heat the tube for 1 minute at 95°C on a heating block.

steps.title: Prepare RT-qPCR Reaction
steps.instruction: Set up the reaction tubes for amplification.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 7.5 µL viral RNA sample solution (which can be stored at -20°C for 14 days) and 7.5 µL OnsiteGene Hi-Sense TM COVID-19 detection kit reaction mix (containing primers and probes) into a superfast RT-qPCR reaction tube.
Secure the lid of the tube.
Spin down the tube for 15 seconds using a centrifuge or spinner.

steps.title: Run RT-qPCR Instrument
steps.instruction: Load and run the samples on the OnsiteGene XDive Superfast Real-Time PCT instrument.

substeps.instruction: Load up to 16 superfast RT-qPCR reaction tubes onto the instrument.

Run the following conditions: Step 1: 50°C for 30 sec; Step 2: 95°C for 0 sec; Step 3: 60°C for 2 sec; Step 4: Read Fluorescence intensity and overhead (10 sec); Step 5: Repeat steps 2-4 for 40 cycles.

steps.title: Post-Processing and Cleanup
steps.instruction: Sterilize materials and document the collection.

substeps.instruction: Sterilize the tube surface with 70% ethanol or a disinfecting wipe.
Place the sample in a secondary container or an appropriately labeled biohazard bag.
Dispose of gloves.
Register the sample collection information, including date and time.

steps.title: Interpret Results
steps.instruction: Report results based on the following CT criteria:

substeps.instruction: Negative: IC CT ≤ 40 AND SARS-Cov-2 Target (ORF1ab/N1) CT > 40.
Positive: IC CT any value AND any SARS-Cov-2 target CT ≤ 40.
Invalid: IC CT > 35 AND SARS-Cov-2 Target (ORF1ab/N1) CT > 40 (indicates IC failure or insufficient specimen volume; retest sample).
Suggestive: One SARS-Cov-2 target positive (CT ≤ 40) and one SARS-Cov-2 target negative (CT > 40).
